claim_1.claim: CyTOF analysis of PBMCs from 52 COVID-19 patients and 62 healthy controls showed a significant reduction in the frequency of plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) and decreased pS6 signaling in pDCs of infected individuals.

sources.quote: There were several differences, but notably the frequency of plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) was significantly reduced in the PBMCs of SARS-CoV-2–infected individuals in both cohorts.
Additionally, there was reduced expression of pS6 [(phosphorylated ribosomal protein S6), a canonical target of mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) activation (15)] in pDCs.

We used mass cytometry to assess immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection in 52 COVID-19 patients, who were confirmed positive for viral RNA by polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and 62 age- and gender-matched healthy controls distributed between the two cohorts.

comparison.finding: significant reduction in the frequency of plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) and decreased pS6 signaling in pDCs of infected individuals

claim_2.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from COVID-19 patients showed reduced production of IFN-a and TNF-a in response to TLR stimulation in pDCs compared to healthy controls.

sources.quote: Consistent with our hypothesis, there was reduced production of IFN-a in response to the TLR stimuli in the pDCs of infected individuals compared with those of healthy controls.
The TNF-a response was also significantly reduced in the pDCs of infected individuals, which demonstrates that the pDCs are functionally impaired in COVID-19 infection.

comparison.finding: reduced production of IFN-a and TNF-a in response to TLR stimulation in pDCs

claim_3.claim: ELISA analysis of plasma from COVID-19 patients showed increased levels of TNFSF14, EN-RAGE, and OSM, which correlated with disease severity.

sources.quote: In addition to IL-6 and other cytokines described previously (10), we identified three proteins that were significantly enhanced in COVID-19 infection and strongly correlated with clinical severity (Fig. 3, bottom row). These were TNFSF14 [LIGHT, a ligand of lymphotoxin B receptor that is highly expressed in human lung fibroblasts and implicated in lung tissue fibrosis and remodeling and inflammation (20)], EN-RAGE [S100A12, a biomarker of pulmonary injury that is implicated in pathogenesis of sepsis-induced ARDS (21)], and oncostatin M [(OSM), a regulator of IL-6].

Given the pronounced and unappreciated observations of the enhanced plasma concentrations of TNFSF14, EN-RAGE, and OSM and their correlation to disease severity, we used an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) to independently validate these results.

comparison.finding: increased levels of TNFSF14, EN-RAGE, and OSM correlated with disease severity

claim_4.claim: RNA sequencing analysis of PBMCs from 17 COVID-19 patients and 17 healthy controls showed an early, transient induction of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) in COVID-19 patients, despite impaired type I IFN production.

sources.quote: We observed a strong induction of the ISGs in COVID-19 subjects compared with healthy donors in this dataset as well (Fig. 4G).
Although the ISG signature shows a strong temporal dependence in our datasets, we also find that the ISG signature is strongly induced in patients with moderate COVID-19 infection (Fig. 4G).

comparison.finding: early, transient induction of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) in COVID-19 patients, despite impaired type I IFN production
